title: Fourth moments of linear forms and centered squares
statement: For every natural number $n$ and every coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb{R}^n$, let $X$ be uniformly distributed on $\{-1,1\}^n$ and let $L_a(X)=\sum_{i=1}^n a_iX_i$. Then $\mathbb{E}[L_a(X)^4]\le 9\bigl(\mathbb{E}[L_a(X)^2]\bigr)^2$. Also, writing $C_a(X)=L_a(X)^2-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2$, one has $\mathbb{E}[C_a(X)^4]\le 81\bigl(\mathbb{E}[C_a(X)^2]\bigr)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ is an arbitrary real coefficient vector indexed by $n$ coordinates
$X$ is uniformly distributed on the Boolean cube
